characters.name: Blossom
characters.description: Blossom is the redhead in the pink outfit and signature red bow. She's the "smart one" and the leader of the team, although at times she can be bossy or over-analytical, and represents "everything nice". Her unique ability, introduced in the episode "Ice Sore", isice breath. Adorably Precocious Child: A 5-year-old who is extremely intelligent for her age. Arch-Enemy: Mojo Jojo for his focus on intelligence, similar to her, and Brick of the Rowdyruff Boys for being her evil counterpart. Badass Bookworm: The most knowledge-oriented sibling of this crime fighting trio. Berserk Button:Don't mess with her hair.In the comic "Bow Jest" messing with her bow will not end well for you.Also, in "Bow Jest", it's shown that making fun of how dependent she is on her bow will make her snap.

characters.name: Bubbles
characters.description: Bubbles is the one in the blue outfit with the blonde hair and pigtails. As the "sugar", she's the most childish, naïve, timid and paranoid of the three, but also the most gentle, caring, and playful. That said, none of that means she's totally harmless and she can still give a beatdown as good as her sisters, especially if she gets mad. She's aFriend to All Living Things, and she has the unique ability totalk to animals and speak any language. Achievements in Ignorance: She scored 1075 on a test in "Him Diddle Riddle" simply by drawing on it. Actress Allusion: When Femme Fatale challenges the Powerpuff Girls to name some memorable superheroines, Bubbles mentionsSupergirlandBatgirl. Bubbles's voice actress,Tara Strong, voiced Batgirl inThe New Batman Adventuressome time earlier. Annoying Younger Sibling: Although all three Girls are the exact same age, she sometimes annoys Blossom and/or Buttercup with her ditzy behavior, albeitunintentionally. All Girls Want Bad Boys: ADownplayedexample, but it's hinted at one point that she might have a crush on Boomer, since she called him "cute" and was the most eager of the girls to kiss her counterpart.Blossom:[Referring to the boys]Let's give ‘em some sugar.Bubbles:[In excitement]OOH! OOH! I WANT THE BLONDE! I THINK HE'S CUTE!

characters.name: Buttercup
characters.description: Buttercup has the green outfit and black hair. She's a tomboy, and the most aggressive and confrontational of the girls, representing "spice". She has gained a reputation among the bad guys of Townsville as the most vicious of the trio, always ready to brawl. Unlike her sisters, she doesn't have a unique ability (to her chagrin). Added Alliterative Appeal: "So we have Blossom, Bubbles, and, hmmm, Buttercup because... it also begins with a B." Makes it 10x sadder when you see herinstantreaction. Annoying Younger Sibling: All three Girls were born at the same exact time, but she sometimes acts as this for Blossom because of her recklessness and how she sometimes teases her. Aloof Big Sister: None of the girls are older or younger than each other, but Buttercup is rather cold, particularly to Bubbles. All Girls Want Bad Boys: She spends "Buttercrush" attracted to Ace, of the Gangreen Gang.

characters.name: Professor Utonium
characters.description: Professor Utonium is the brilliant scientist who created the girls in his lab. He acts as a father figure, caring for them as a single parent would. He's enthusiastic about his work and cooks up all sorts of inventions and experiments in his lab. Achievements in Ignorance: Every time he makes something useful, it was by accident:Dynamo doesn't count as an exception, because even though he made it on purpose, it caused disaster.The one proper exception is in the episode "Nano of the North", where his purposefully built shrink ray was crucial in helping the girls save the day. Even though in the end he ended up saving the day by stepping on the monster, it never would've gotten to that point had he not shrunk the girls down. The girls were then able to destroy most of the nanobots causing the remaining few to combine in desperation. Dynamo doesn't count as an exception, because even though he made it on purpose, it caused disaster. Even though in the end he ended up saving the day by stepping on the monster, it never would've gotten to that point had he not shrunk the girls down. The girls were then able to destroy most of the nanobots causing the remaining few to combine in desperation. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: In "Knock It Off" when Dick Hardly has the girls trapped and is draining them of their chemical X, which is killing them, and there's nothing he can do about it. It doesn't work.

characters.name: Bunny
characters.description: A fourth Powerpuff Girl that Blossom, Bubbles and Buttercup create in "Twisted Sister". Unfortunately, she causes more harm than good. Acrofatic: Bunny is wider compared to the rest of the Girls but still just as strong and quick as they are. Beware the Nice Ones: She defeats criminals by herself when they assault the Girls. Beware the Silly Ones: She's mentally slow but manages to beat up crooks that were attacking the Girls all on her own. Big Little Sister: She's technically the youngest of the Girls (as well as their creation) but also the tallest and bulkiest.

characters.name: Bullet
characters.description: Abnormal Ammo: She can gather nuts inside her mouth and spit them at her enemies. Action Pet: Definitely counts as one for the girls when they merely adopted her as their own pet, became a member of their team, and engaged in everyday heroic duties alongside them. But this eventually didn't stick for long, mainly because she felt homesick and wanted to stay at her original home after protecting the animals. Ambiguous Gender: Her gender isn't properly confirmed in her debut episode, but she is consistently addressed with feminine pronouns, but was called a boy by Buttercup. She also has an ambigous-looking face. Animal Superhero: Oh yes. Badass Adorable: A little squirrel with a Powerpuff-like face who is just as strong and badass as the girls that looked after her.

characters.name: The Run-of-the-Mill Girls
characters.description: Mundane versions of the Powerpuff Girls dreamed by Professor Utonium in "Oops, I Did It Again", when he realized that all his most successful creations were partly or entirely the result of unintended accidents and thought how the Powerpuff Girls could have been like had they still been made of sugar, spice and everything nice, but without the dose of Chemical X. Their individual names are Bertha (Blossom's counterpart), Beatrice (Bubbles) and Betty (Buttercup). Dream People: They're non-existent characters imagined by Professor Utonium in a dream. Mythology Gag: Their designs are directly ripped from redesigns of the Powerpuff Girls thatCraig McCrackenhad once considered using for the series itself following the criticism towards the girls' initial and eventual final designs that theWhat a Cartoon!pilots received. Non-Standard Character Design: Downplayed. While they have more proportioned bodies and faces, and actual noses, fingers and toes in contrast to the Powerpuff Girls, their design style looks like something out of a90sto early2000sanimated kids' show, unlike the rest of the cast'sHanna-Barberaand mid-20th century cartoon-inspired designs.

characters.name: In General
characters.description: A team ofmale counterpartsof the Powerpuff Girls, created by Mojo Jojo out of snips, snails, and The Talking Dog’s tail flushed down the water of a prison toilet with Chemical X. They love causing mayhem, mischief, and chaos. They were originally one-off villains with little-to-no personality, killed off in the same Season 1 episode (also titled "The Rowdyruff Boys") they were introduced, but they quickly became a fan favorite and were later resurrected by HIM in the Season 5 episode "The Boys are Back in Town" to become recurring members of the girls'Rogues Gallerywith visual redesigns and full-fledged characterization. Acquired Achilles' Heel: When the girls first fought the Rowdyruff Boys, they defeated them by kissing them due toGirls Have Cooties. After HIM brings themBack from the Dead, they not onlydon't have the weakness, but actually growstrongerfrom being kissed. However, the girls discovered that they gained a new weakness ofbecoming smaller and weaker when they feel emasculated, which the girls exploit to reduce them to the size of ants. All Girls Want Bad Boys: The teenage versions of the girls seen in a flashback from "The City of Clipsville" certainly think this of them.Teenage Bubbles: We shouldn't talk to them! They'rebad!Teenage Blossom and Buttercup:(dreamily)Iknow.... Always Someone Better: While not necessarily "better", the Girls simplycannottake the Rowdyruff Boys on in a straight fight. Every time, they have to resort to a clever tactic to outsmart them. Part of this is they're roughly equal in power, but the Rowdyruff Boys aren't concerned about leveling the city going all out. Anime Hair: When they come back. Lampshaded by Buttercup.

characters.name: Mojo Jojo
characters.description: AMad Scientistchimpanzee with great intelligence, a pseudo-Japanese accent, and a convoluted, repetitive manner of speaking (inspired by the speech patterns of characters in the English dub ofSpeed RacerandThe Super Dictionary). As revealed in the episode "Mr. Mojo's Rising", and expanded upon inThe Powerpuff Girls Movie, Mojo Jojo was originally Professor Utonium's reckless lab assistant, Jojo, before Professor Utonium created the Powerpuff Girls, and it was he who caused the Professor to accidentally add Chemical X to the mixture, thus making him responsible for their creation. The reason he hates the girls so much is out of envy of the affection they received from the Professor that he did not. To listen to Mojo himself list these tropes,click here. Accidental Hero: In "Just Another Manic Mojo". Mojo tried to kill the Powerpuff Girls, while having them sit and wait, as he claims to find their ball. However, he grows so frustrated by The Powerpuff Girls sticking their nose in everything in his lair, that he gives them the ball, only so he can get rid of them. The next day, the newspaper declares him a hero for giving them their ball back. The Ace: That big brain of his isn’t just for show. He can create amazingly built inventions like giant robots and hi-tech guns effortlessly, is a fully trained hibachi chef, took the Gangreen Gang out with a trash can lid, beat a giant alien overlord with his bare hands and no backup, and built a machine that alters reality. Aesop Amnesia: About half of his failures to destroy the girls would be reduced if he would just simply take the time to plan his schemes carefully in order to circumvent any major flaw he often overlooks.

characters.name: HIM
characters.description: A mysterious, effeminate (apparently androgynous), and immortal caricature ofSatan. He is the ultimate embodiment of evil, and talks in a chilling voice that echoes at all times as if in a cave; the voice itself can vary from a high-pitched, effeminate falsetto voice, to a deep, roaring demonic voice. He is also the Girls' most dangerous foe as well as the hardest villain to defeat. He's one of the girls' main enemies but in particular an enemy for Bubbles. Agent Peacock: His slim build, feminine clothing, high-pitched voice, and love of things like pampering himself in the tub and doing Jazzercise suggest that he's a silly, lighthearted villain.He isn't. Ambiguous Gender: There's been a lot of confusion about what sex HIM really is, but he has universally been referred to with male pronouns and identifies as such in the show. He also has a beard and was seen bare-chested in "Tough Love". And, well, his name isHIM, for more reasons than one.The narrator, during the 2009 marathon leading up to the premiere of "Powerpuff Girls Rule!", lampshaded this, and eventually settled on calling him "HERM". The narrator, during the 2009 marathon leading up to the premiere of "Powerpuff Girls Rule!", lampshaded this, and eventually settled on calling him "HERM". Ambiguously Gay: He wears a lot of feminine clothing and speaks in an effeminate voice (at least until he gets angry); also, helicks the Professor's facein the episode "Tough Love". To say nothing of the episode 'Custody Battle' where he and Mojo Jojo argue over who would be a better parent to the Rowdyruff Boys. The episode ends with the two of them embracing on a hill and watching the boys fly into the sunset.

characters.name: Fuzzy Lumpkins
characters.description: A large, husky, furry, pink, and bear-like hillbilly monster with a wide jaw, a green nose, two antennae on his head, bib blue overalls, and brown countryman shoes. He talks with a Southern accent, and will shoot anything he finds trespassing on his property, but is otherwise harmless. He lives in the woods next to the city of Townsville. He is also prone to destructive fits of rage, during which he gains enough physical strength to overpower (and sometimes intimidate) the girls, meaning they must outsmart him to beat him. Anti-Villain:He's very dangerous to ordinary folk, but generally he'll leave you alone if you leave him alone, unless he's manipulated by other villains or wanders into the city by mistake.This is averted in later seasons when he's a flat-out villain who goes out of his way to commit crimes. Even the movie prequel depicts him robbing a grocery store cash register with a sinister grin on his face. He's very dangerous to ordinary folk, but generally he'll leave you alone if you leave him alone, unless he's manipulated by other villains or wanders into the city by mistake. This is averted in later seasons when he's a flat-out villain who goes out of his way to commit crimes. Even the movie prequel depicts him robbing a grocery store cash register with a sinister grin on his face. Art Evolution:In "Meat Fuzzy Lumpkins", Fuzzy was notably taller and had more human-like proportions compared to the more ball-shaped body he would take on in the show.

characters.name: Princess Morbucks
characters.description: Abusive Offspring: Downplayed. She doesn'tabuseher father so much as she just whines and begs him to buy or do things for hernoteHe actually tapped a rolled-up newspaper against his palm on one occasion, implying hedoesdiscipline her to some extent. On the other hand, she is downrightcruelto her own mother, as evidenced when she lets out a long insult tirade towards her over the phone. Alpha Bitch: She's a rich, spoiled Prima Donna that thinks she's better than the girls (and, by extension, everyone else). However, the trope is ultimately subverted since she's really not that popular and none of her schoolmates actually like or trust her. Artistic License – Law: Everytime Princess gets arrested, she's often sent to prison. In real life, minors like her should actually be taken to juvenile detention centers, the youth equivalent to jails. Then again, considering who runs the city of Townsville... Attention Whore: Quite possibly the biggest reason Princess wanted to be a Powerpuff Girl in the first place is that she wanted to be more recognized by everyone else than she was before, given herhighly rich statuscoming from her father. Badass Adorable: A 5-year-old girl who's a competent fighter and has enough expensive, high-tech gear to match the Powerpuff Girls.

characters.name: Sedusa
characters.description: A master (or rather, mistress) of disguise who uses her cunning and her sex appeal to trick powerful men into doing her bidding. True to herPunny Name, she hasPrehensile Hair, which is her greatest asset in combat. Advertised Extra: Was consistently featured in promo material as a major part of theRogues Gallery, but she made very few appearances in the series, and was effectively replaced as the primary female villain by Princess Morbucks from Season 2 onwards. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: After her defeat in "Something's A Ms.", she desperately begs Ms. Bellum not to cut off all her hair. Amazing Technicolor Population: She has chalk-white skin. Ambiguously Human: She has a fairly human appearance, with the exception of herwhite skin, unusual hair powers, and when we see her hair being completely shaved off in "Aspirations",Pointy Ears. Given hername, she is likely some sort of gorgon, but this goes unspecified in-series.

characters.name: Ace
characters.description: The leader of the Gangreen Gang, who's responsible for scheming most of their criminal escapades and has a decent charisma that allows him to manipulate other people. Benevolent Boss: Despite often punching Snake, Ace shows care and appreciation for the rest of the gang. He considers Grubber's advice, helps Arturo reach high places, and comforts Billy whenever he cries. Blatant Lies: In "Buttercrush", he tries to convince the girls that one of his friends didn't know what they did was wrong and that he is sorry. And at the end of the episode, right after Buttercup realizes her sisters are in danger, Ace tries to pin the blame on the rest of the gang, claiming they put him up to it. Buttercup doesn't buy it that time. Cue epic ass-kicking. Brooklyn Rage: He's got a slight New York-inspired accent and is a dangerous foe. The Charmer: Ace can be very charismatic when he wants to be.

characters.name: Snake
characters.description: Full name Sanford Ingleberry, Snake is the Gangreen Gang's second-in-command, who's defined by his snake-like appearance and motif. He has the role of the gang's resident mischievous trickster and stealth operator, though his position and occasional stupidity make him mostly a yes-man to Ace. Ambiguously Human: In addition to having the same green skin as the rest of the gang, he has distinctively serpentine features, including a forked tongue. Butt-Monkey: He is constantlyuppercuttedby Ace. Even in "Buttercrush", Ace and Buttercup use him as a walking punching bag. Chainsaw Good: In the "Whoopass Stew" pilot, he tries to attack the girls using a chainsaw, only for Buttercup to unplug his weapon. Cheated Angle: He is only seen in 3/4 angle and sideways, never in the front.

characters.name: Grubber
characters.description: A physically deformed guy with a hunchbacked body, eyes that protrude out of his much-larger eye sockets and ragged clothes. Because his tongue hangs out of his mouth most of the time, his speech is usually limited to blowing raspberries, though he's also capable of imitating other people's voices perfectly. Bad "Bad Acting": His impersonation of Buttercup in "Buttercrush" sounds nothing like her, which even has the audience wondering how Bubbles and especially Blossom were fooled in the slightest. It's averted after this though. Barefoot Loon: He is always barefoot, probably to emphasize his already gross and bizarre appearance. Blowing a Raspberry: This is how he communicates, and somehow, Ace understands exactly what he's saying. Body Horror: His hunchback appearance makes him look downright terrifying!

characters.name: Big Billy
characters.description: Full name William W. Williams, Big Billy is the gang's largest yet most idiotic member, being delegated mostly to the role of muscle. He's far kinder and and more childish than his teammates. Affably Evil: He's easily the nicest member of the gang. In one episode, Big Billy is very friendly to the Girls when they save him. Can't Take Criticism: He certainly didn't take it well when Blossom finally called him out on his inadvertent destruction in an attempt at heroism. Cyclops: He reveals in "Schoolhouse Rocked" that he has only a single eye. A Day in the Limelight: Big Billy is the only gang member to get an episode primarily revolved around him: "Slave the Day."

characters.name: Lil' Arturo
characters.description: Full name Arturo de la Guerra, Lil' Arturo is the Hispanic, shortest member of the Gangreen Gang, with his height being just a little taller than the average kindergarterner. He's the least-fledged member of the group in terms of character, being mostly defined as a somewhat immature yet willing delinquent. Be the Ball: This often happens to him. He's been thrown by Grubber as a projectile against the girls in the "Whoopass Stew" pilot, used as a volleyball by Blossom and Bubbles in "Buttercrush", a baseball by Fuzzy and Mojo in "Telephonies", and a basketball by Big Billy in "Schoolhouse Rocked." Cheated Angle: Arturo's bang switches sides whenever he faces an opposite direction. Depraved Dwarf: He's the gang's smallest member, and he's just as cruel and nasty as them as well. Evil Sounds Raspy: Arturo is in aGang of Bulliesand he speaks in a raspy Hispanic accent.

characters.name: The Amoeba Boys
characters.description: The Amoeba Boys are a trio of human-sized anthropomorphic protozoan gangsters. They'd like to be the greatest criminals Townsville has ever seen, but their brains aren't developed enough to come up with any schemes more evil thanpetty shoplifting or littering. The Powerpuff Girls consider them harmless, to their dismay—they'd consider it a badge of honor if they were evil enough to get beaten up by the Girls. Ironically, they've come closer to destroying Townsville and defeating the Powerpuff Girls than most of the other villains combined—all by accident, of course. Affably Evil: The Amoeba Boys are quite friendly and affable to the girls, even to the point of calling themselves their best friends in "Birthday Bash". The only reason they commit crimes is mostly because they want to be seen as criminals by the girls. Big Bad Wannabe: Theywantto be renowned villains, but of course, all they can come up with is minor crimes that police wouldn't even care to ticket someone for. Big, Thin, Short Trio: Bossman is the Big, Slim is theThin, and Junior is the Short. Blob Monster: They were created out of water.

characters.name: Brick
characters.description: The leader of the Rowdyruff Boys and Blossom's counterpart, who represents "puppy dog's tail". In contrast to Blossom's pink color and red bow, Brick is design-wise defined by a bright red outfit and backwards baseball cap. Initially having a fairly goal-focused personality without much taunting in the boys' debut, their return made him arrogant and hot-headed in his disposition. He's not academically smart like Blossom, but shows a knowledge of team fighting and street tactics. Big Brother Bully: Both he and Butch enjoy picking on Boomer. Big "SHUT UP!": In "The Boys Are Back in Town", Brick angrily tells the Powerpuff Girls to be silent after the Girls mocked the Boys' current appearances. In "Custody Battle", when Mojo and HIM still heatedly argue over the Rowdyruff Boys, Brick, alongside Boomer and Butch, grow agitated and furiously yells at his "fathers" to shut up and cease their bickering competition. Cowardly Lion: While he may has a cunning knowledge, he still shows to be quite fearful. Dope Slap: Gives these toBoomera lot, starting in "The Boys are Back in Town."

characters.name: Boomer
characters.description: Bubbles' Rowdyruff counterpart, who represents "snips" and is identified with a darker shade of blue than that of Bubbles. He's considerably more irrational and idiotic than Bubbles while lacking most of her sensitivity. Affably Evil: He's nicer than his brothers, at least. But that's only in comparison. Annoying Younger Sibling: Technically the boys were created at the same time, but he is thematically youngest just like his counterpart, and his idiocy irritates Brick and Butch. Big "SHUT UP!": In "Custody Battle", when Mojo and HIM still heatedly argue over the Rowdyruff Boys, Boomer, alongside Brick and Butch, grow agitated and furiously yells at his "fathers" to shut up and cease their bickering competition. Beware the Silly Ones: Boomer may be an idiot, but he still causes lots of damage like his brothers.

characters.name: Butch
characters.description: Buttercup's Rowdyruff counterpart, who represents "snails" and has a darker shade of green than Buttercup's as his signature color. Contrasting with Buttercup's jerkishness and passion for brawling but otherwise contained, firmly heroic demeanor when neither trait are necessarily called into play, Butch is extremely unhinged and hyperactive with a huge penchant for violence and destruction. Ax-Crazy: All of the Boys are, but Butch is downrightbatshit insane. Big Brother Bully: Like the Girls, all three of them are the same age, but Boomernotethe counterpart of Bubbles, who is thematically considered the baby sister.is treated as the youngest and frequently gets bullied by Butch and Brick. Big "SHUT UP!": In "Custody Battle", when Mojo and HIM still heatedly argue over the Rowdyruff Boys, Butch, alongside Brick and Boomer, grow agitated and furiously yells at his "fathers" to shut up and cease their bickering competition. Blood Knight: To anAx-Crazyextent.

characters.name: The Narrator
characters.description: The series' enthusiastic narrator is never seen at any point in the series, though he is a person and not just a disembodied voice—for example, in "Monkey See, Doggie Do", he's turned into a dog along with the rest of Townsville, and in "Simian Says", Mojo Jojo kidnaps him and takes his place as the narrator. As the narrator, he, of course, has the ability tobreak the fourth wall. Breaking the Fourth Wall: Will often be part of the story despite being just a voice. Catchphrase: States "The city of Townsville!" almost every episode and "So Once Again, the Day Is Saved, thanks to The Powerpuff Girls!" (or some variation of it) at the end. A Day in the Limelight: There is an episode where he is kidnapped by Mojo Jojo and needs to be saved, because the narration has the power to control the show. Demoted to Extra: In the 2016 reboot, his role was way less prominent than in the original 1998 series, only showing up in a few episodes before beingremoved all togetherhalfway through season one.

characters.name: The Mayor of Townsville
characters.description: The mayor of Townsville wears a trademark hat, monocle, and huge bushy mustache, and isreferred to only as "Mayor"(even campaigning with the slogan "vote for Mayor for Mayor"). He is neitherbrightnormature, and relies heavily on his secretary and personal assistant, Ms. Sara Bellum, to do the real work around the place.The Mayor seems to have his job only because no one bothers to run against him; The Narrator once refers to him as "The Pity of Townsville." Also,he really likes pickles, butdoes NOT like people wearing his hat. Balloon Belly: In "Candy is Dandy", he gets one after eating a lot of candy. Berserk Button:In "Impeach Fuzz", Fuzzy Lumpkins finds out the hard way what happens when you wear the Mayor's hat.As seen in in the film hereallydoesn't like it if you destroy his favorite pickle stand, and wanted to have the girls run out of town when they accidentally did so during their game of tag. In "Impeach Fuzz", Fuzzy Lumpkins finds out the hard way what happens when you wear the Mayor's hat. As seen in in the film hereallydoesn't like it if you destroy his favorite pickle stand, and wanted to have the girls run out of town when they accidentally did so during their game of tag.

characters.name: Sara Bellum
characters.description: Ms. Bellum is the mayor's much-more-competent personal assistant, helping him out with whatever he can't handle on his own (i.e. just about everything). What's infamous about her is that her face has never been shown, as it always blocked by the top of the frame, a conveniently-placed obstacle, or something like that. Action Girl: She is one of the most accomplished martial artists in the series, capable of going toe to toe with Sedusa. Ambiguously Brown: She's noticeably darker than most of the cast, though it's unknown if it's simply a tan or a hint for her indication (since she is heavily implied to be a Latina). In the DC Comicsseries, she has caucasian coloring in what is probably an error. Badass Normal: She managed to defeat Sedusa, a supervillainess with hair powers, in a fight.. Beauty Equals Goodness: She's the show's beautifulFanservice-providingfemale character, but what makes her stand out is how she's both heroicandkind-naturedto everyone.

characters.name: Miss Keane
characters.description: The kindergarten teacher of Pokey Oaks Kindergarten. She is patient, understanding and very protective of her students, making her a well-liked, motherly figure. Art Evolution:Received a large amount of changes for the final seasons of the original series. Note that she has much larger eyes and permanent eyebrows, and her lipstick is less prominent. Received a large amount of changes for the final seasons of the original series. Note that she has much larger eyes and permanent eyebrows, and her lipstick is less prominent. Berserk Button: Never say anything mean about cats. She even gets upset if you tell her you don't like cats. Cool Teacher: You kind of have to be one to deal with the Powerpuff Girls.

characters.name: Mitch Mitchelson
characters.description: A mean kid who is in the girls' kindergarten class. Alliterative Name:MitchMitchelson. Ax-Crazy: If you paid attention to detail and seen what his room looks like, you'd quickly know why. Berserk Button: He does not like to be called by his real name "Mitchell". Black Bead Eyes: His eyes are drawn this way.

characters.name: Elmer Sglue
characters.description: A kindergarten boy who turned into a giant glue monster. Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever: After eating paste that a radioactive bug gets into. Butt-Monkey: Before turning into a giant paste monster, he was the butt of many jokes from the other kids, including Buttercup. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Doesn't appear in the 2016 show outside of a flashback to the original show. Extreme Omnivore: Comes with being aPaste Eater.

characters.name: Mike Believe
characters.description: A shy boy in Pokey Oaks Kindergarten who creates an imaginary friend called Patches. Unfortunately, Patches causes a lot of mischief. Cassandra Truth: Blames much of the problems that happen after he shows up on Patches. No one believes him until the invisible Patches' actions are witnessed firsthand. Expy:Inverted, he was likely an inspiration forMac. I Just Want to Have Friends: Mike’s reason for creating Patches. At the end of the episode, Bubbles offers to be Mike’s friend. One-Shot Character: Never appeared again since "Imaginary Fiend", except for a cameo appearance in aFoster's Home for Imaginary Friendscomic where an imaginary doppleganger of Frankie he created is dropped off at the house.

characters.name: Harry Pitt
characters.description: A dirty, unkempt classmate of the girls at Pokey Oak, who is said to have cooties. Abhorrent Admirer: Harry is this to the girls, due to his unkempt appearance and the belief that he has cooties. Mojo Jojo uses this to his advantage by recruiting the boy so the girls won't interfere with his crimes. This becomes averted once the girls learn that cooties aren't real. His episode ends with him getting smooched up by the girls until his face is covered in red lipstick marks. Affectionate Nickname: He is called a "Cutie" by the girls before they give him a big smooching. All Abusers Are Male: While he isn't downright malicious himself, his own affectionate approach towards any girl he sees (including the Powerpuff Girls themselves) still has him being a fair example for this trope. Mojo Jojo even exploits such approach of his (up until it backfired). Amazon Chaser: While he seems to go after any female he encounters, Harry ends up taking a particular interest in the three heroines when Mojo recruits him.

characters.name: Mr. Green
characters.description: A monster who works as a substitute teacher for Miss Keane's class the one time she's absent in the "Substitute Creature" episode. The girls are distrustful of him due to his nature but it soon becomes apparent that his ugly exterior belies his kind personality. Beauty Equals Goodness: He's quite possibly the single-most human-looking monster in the show and tends to make a lot of cute expressions, and is one of the nicest characters. Cute Monster Guy: He's one of the most human looking monsters in the show and is endearing due to how nice and sweet of a person he is. Dark Is Not Evil: He turns out to be a rather nice guy despite his off-putting appearance. Face of a Thug: Downplayed. His green skin, horns, eyepatch, and scar, plus his outfit, make him look like an evil supervillain, but he also has a kind face and a tendency to make a lot of cute expressions.

characters.name: Talking Dog
characters.description: As one can readily deduce, the Talking Dog is a canine resident of Townsville who has the inexplicable ability to speak English. Brutal Honesty: In "Shut The Pup Up", he doesn't sugarcoat any of the somewhat crass things he says. Butt-Monkey: Gets his share of bad luck. He's constantly abused in almost every episode he appears in. Cartoon Dog Breed: A white dog with black ears and tail and a single black spot on his back. He looks a lot likeSnoopyand has no breed given. Disproportionate Retribution: In "Bubblevicious", when Bubbles is going crazy over everyone treating her like she'sJust a Kidand "cute little Bubbles", she beats up the Talking Dog for causing a traffic jam.Talking Dog: No...Bubbles, have mercy...Bubbles: Mercy is for theweak!

characters.name: Daddy Morbucks
characters.description: Princess' father. He never says anything in the series, but he is known for spoiling his daughter rotten. Corrupted Character Copy: Just as his daughter is a far more unscrupulous and bratty version ofLittle Orphan Annie, he's a less benign ersatz of Annie's adoptive father Daddy Warbucks in that he focuses on spoiling Princess rotten rather than actually disciplining his daughter when she misbehaves and doesn't even try to connect to his child in a way that doesn't involve showering her with money and material things. The Faceless: He is only shown from below the neck. Hands-Off Parenting: His parenting boils down to throwing money at his daughter to shut her up. Hypocrite: He never punishes Princess whenever she commits crimes against the girls and Townsville, but he only punished Princess in "Bought and Scold" when her actions (indirectly getting his house robbed) inconvenienced him.

characters.name: The Mayor's Wife
characters.description: She's, well,the Mayor's wife. The Mayor doesn't seem to like her very much. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: She eventually stopped showing up or being mentioned, although she does appear for a few seconds in "Reeking Havoc". Possibly doubles asEarly-Installment Weirdness, as subsequent episodes imply that the Mayor is single. Growling Gut: Her stomach bubbles while in bed in "Reeking Havoc". Look-Alike Lovers: As you can see in her picture, she looks exactly like a female version of The Mayor. No Name Given: Her real name is never revealed, she's only referred to as "The Mayor's Wife".

characters.name: Captain Righteous And Lefty
characters.description: Arch-Enemy: Were this to the Ministry of Pain, Mastermind especially. Batman Parody: Lefty's costume is identical to that of Batman's sidekick Robin, only colored red, white and blue instead of red, black and green and with an L insignia instead of an R. Big "NO!": Righteous' reaction when Lefty is shoved to the ground by Mastermind and breaks his hip. Fan Disservice: During theLock-and-Load Montage, we get a good look at Righteous trying to cram his sagging, elderly body back into his old costume. It's not a pleasant sight. Feeling Their Age: Just like their old enemies, the former heroes are much weaker, slower and more fragile than they used to be, and while they dotechnicallysave the day once again, it's aPyrrhic Victoryat best that lands everyone involved in the hospital.

characters.name: Robin Snyder
characters.description: A little girl that the Girls befriend in "Super Friends", after she moves in next door to them. All for Nothing: Turns out that she only befriended Princess out of the latter's manipulation, leaving their relationship with each other in vain. All-Loving Hero: She's a loving girl towards anyone whom she meets, regardless of their morality. She didn't seem to hold much of a grudge towards Princess when she betrayed her and just genuinely wanted to be friends with theSpoiled Brat. Ambiguous Situation: Whatdoesit really mean when she refers to herself as an "accident"? Bound and Gagged: Princess ties her up and gags herafter tricking her into stealing candy so that she could pretend to catch her in the act and look like a hero, in order to convince the girls to accept her as a PPG.

characters.name: Stan and Sandra Practice
characters.description: Actor Allusion: Stan wears green, Sandra has blonde hair and wears a pink shirt, and both are voiced byDaran NorrisandSusanne Blakesleerespectively, which should easily compare them toCosmo and Wanda. Alliterative Family: Both of their names start with an "S". Big Bad Duumvirate: Of their debut episode "Girls Gone Mild". And then the Dooks of Doom arrive to take over and cause mayhem. Deconstruction: OfMoral Guardians. Them forbidding the Powerpuff Girls from using their superpowers or fighting crime out of a personal distate for violence, even though the girls are the most effective and competent superheroines in Townsville, and their contract winds up doing more harm than good for the people of Townsville due to it allowing regular crooks and supervillains a-like to run rampant. Godzilla Threshold: It takes Dooks of Doom barraging into their house and literallytrying to eat themfor them to relent and allow the girls to fight crime again.

characters.name: Giant Monsters
characters.description: Stock monsters that appear in many episodes to terrorize Townsville for the girls to defeat. Some monsters play important roles in a few episodes, such as the Blowfish facing DYNAMO in "Uh Oh Dynamo". A Hero to His Hometown: Monsters don't getany respecton Monster Isle unless they fight the girls and survive, whereupon they are celebrated as a hero. Always a Bigger Fish: A literal example. The giant Blowfish has abigger brother that the Powerpuffs need to pilot the DYNAMO to stop. Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever: All of the monsters are massive in size, and are able to destroy buildings with ease. Expy:One of the recurring stock monsters resembles Gyango fromUltraman.Steve in "Super Zeroes" resemblesHedorah.

characters.name: Roach Coach
characters.description: One of the first villains introduced in the show, who stars in the episode "Insect Inside". Roach Coach uses a whistle to summon an army of cockroaches to attack Townsville. Advertised Extra: Roach Coach appeared in numerous promotional materials and animated bumpers during the show's original run, and even appears in the villain lineup in the intro and is mentioned by name in the ending theme song. Despite this, he only had one starring episode, made a non-speaking cameo appearance in two others, and appeared on a wanted poster in another. Big Creepy-Crawlies: Becomes this when he fuses with his army. The Cameo:He makes a non-speaking cameo in the beginning of "Bought and Scold" while the Narrator is talking about the villains of Townsville.He appears on a wanted poster in the beginning of "Divide and Conquer".He makes a non-speaking cameo in "The Powerpuff Girls Rule" as one of several villains pursuing the Key to the World. He makes a non-speaking cameo in the beginning of "Bought and Scold" while the Narrator is talking about the villains of Townsville.

characters.name: The Powerbluffs
characters.description: Appear only in the episode "Powerpuff Bluff". A trio of criminals who decide to impersonate the Powerpuff Girls in order to escape prison after several failed attempts at robbery. Specifically, the light-skinned, red-headed leader impersonates Blossom, the member who impersonates Bubbles has tan skin and a mohawk, and the member who impersonates Buttercup is a black man. Beard of Evil: Their leader has a beard. Evil Redhead: The leader of the trio is a criminal with red hair, with aBeard of Evilto compliment it. Laughably Evil: They're a trio of burly and hirsute crooks who poorly disguise themselves as the Powerpuff Girls and still manage to fool almost everyone into mistaking them for the real deal. What else would they be besides hilarious? No Name Given: Their actual names are never given.

characters.name: Boogie Man
characters.description: Appears only in the episode "Boogie Frights." He hatches a plan to blanket the world in perpetual night by blocking out the sun with a giant disco ball, so that he and his fellow night-terrors, the Nightmare Monsters, can wreak havoc forever. Advertised Extra: Despite appearing in the villain lineup in the intro (albeit only in the widescreen version shown in "The Powerpuff Girls Rule"), he only has one major appearance and two non-speaking cameos. Back for the Finale: He can be seen in the redone intro for "The Powerpuff Girls Rule", and he and two of his minions make a cameo in the episode itself, pursuing the Key to the World. The Cameo: He makes a non-speaking cameo in the beginning of "Bought and Scold", and as mentioned in "Back For The Finale", he makes another cameo appearance in "The Powerpuff Girls Rule". Classy Cane: The Boogie Man carries a cane with a diamond mounted on the top. It also has a button which he uses to launch the disco ball to block out the sun.

characters.name: Nightmare Monsters
characters.description: The species of monsters led by the Boogie Man from "Boogie Frights". Dem Bones: One of their briefly-seen background members is a living human skeleton who wears orange overalls and black shoes. Kaiju: A lot of them are, inexplicably, the size of buildings or even bigger - at least one is large enough to hold anuclear cooling towerlike a soda can. Yet somehow they all live underneath people's beds. Logical Weakness: Being monsters of the night, it's no wonder that sunlight will kill them outright. Zerg Rush: There are too many of them for the Girls to handle and fighting them becomes a war of attrition they know they'll eventually lose. The only hope of stopping them is toendThe Night That Never Ends.

characters.name: Abracadaver
characters.description: Appearing only in the episode of the same name, Abracadaver was, in life, the magician Al Lusion. Back when the Mayor was a child, Al Lusion dazzled the town with his stagecraft, but died after getting accidentally humiliated by a volunteer resembling Blossom and stumbling into an iron maiden. Many years later, he's freed from the iron maiden, now a zombie wizard hellbent on revenge... Advertised Extra: Despite appearing in the villain lineup in the intro, he only has one major appearance and one non-speaking cameo. Back from the Dead: Was killed in a magic trick gone wrong and came back as a zombie to terrorize Townsville. Berserk Button: Anything resembling the little girl that ruined his career, specifically Blossom. Black and Blue and Scary All Over: He was only seen in grayscale color during the time he was alive, but as a zombie in the present, he has greenish-blue skin that meshes with his predominantly black magician suit. His overall color scheme combines the trope withRed and Black and Evil All Over, as he also hasglowing red eyes, and the scenery in Townsville turns into red and black when he starts tormenting the city.

characters.name: Major Man
characters.description: Appears only in the episode "Major Competition". A hero who shows up in Townsville and appears to outshine the girls in every way. He's not nearly as noble as he pretends to be. The Ace: He appears to be this at first, effortlessly stopping crimes and saving the day. Subverted when it turns out that he's the one causing the crises so that he can show up and solve them. Accidental Public Confession: During a TV interview with the Mayor, the Mayor mentions how quickly Major Man is able to get to the crime scene. Major Man follows by saying that he'd have to know about it in advance, then he takes back what he said giving the girls the idea to expose him. Alliterative Name:MajorMan. Get it? Ambiguously Human: Helookshuman, and his cousin and grandmother appear to be normal humans, but he has genuine superpowers and can breathe in space like the Girls. His origins are never revealed, leaving itup in the airas to what he really is.

characters.name: Mr. Mime
characters.description: Appears only in the episode "Mime for a Change." Mr. Mime is what you get when you douse the local smiling birthday entertainer Rainbow the Clown in bleach. Has nothing to do withthe Pokémonof the same name. Advertised Extra: Despite appearing in the villain lineup in the intro, he only has one major appearance and one non-speaking cameo. Alternate Personality Punishment: After changing Mr. Mime back into Rainbow the Clown, the Powerpuffs beat up Rainbow and send him to jail even though he wasNot Himself. Bald of Evil: Just like Rainbow the Clown, his scalp is bald.UnlikeRainbow, Mr. Mime is an evil supervillain.

characters.name: Lenny Baxter (a.k.a. Lenny the Comic Book Geek)
characters.description: A one-shot antagonist who appears in "Collect Her". He is an obsessive comic book geek and toy collector, who owns every conceivable piece of Powerpuff Girls merchandise in mint condition, and wants to add the real deal to his collection. While he has no superpowers, he was able to lure the girls into his room, capture them and trap them in toy packaging, which prompted the entire town to hunt him down and ruin his mint condition toy collection in front of him in order to get him to free the girls, and he was promptly jailed. Advertised Extra: Despite appearing in the villain lineup in the intro, he only has one major appearance and one non-speaking cameo. And Then What?: His whole plot to kidnap the girls happened because he finally completed his merch collection and didn't know what to do with himself afterward.Lenny:Now what'll I do? Collecting Powerpuff stuff is my life. I've got every piece of merchandise known to man! My collection...is complete! Oh, it's just not enough!!Narrator:Sheesh, buddy! Get a life! Ascended Extra: Oddly, Cartoon Network's Fridays block had him hosting "Betcha Didn't Know" segments, analyzing bits of trivia from various cartoons. These universally portray him asfriendly and humorous, and you'd be forgiven if you forget he once tried to captured the Powerpuff Girls for all eternity. Lenny also makes a cameo in the Cartoon Network cinema bumper, sitting in the movie theater with a bucket of popcorn. Badass Normal: He manages to single-handedly trap the Powerpuff Girls without any kind of powers.

characters.name: The Smiths
characters.description: Appear in the episodes "Supper Villain" and "Just Desserts". The Smiths were an average family living next door to the Powerpuff Girls. Harold Smith had become sickened by his routine life and menial job at a mustard factory. Inspired by Mojo Jojo, he began to embrace the life of a supervillain. Unfortunately, he chose to do this on the night his wife Maryanne invited Professor Utonium and thePPGsto dinner. Everything eventually devolved into a food fight, and the police arrest Harold. Maryanne, however, put a lot of effort into the dinner, and upon seeing it get ruined (and blaming the Powerpuff Girls), she vowed to destroy the Powerpuff Girls. Berserk Button: Donotruin Maryanne's dinner. It's eventually not just pressed, but stabbed in about 100 times. Also, donotlose Julie's jacks. Big Bad Wannabe: Despite their efforts to be real threats towards the Powerpuff Girls on the level of some of Townsville's worst villains, they can only threaten the non-superpowered Professor Utonium genuinely and the second the girls aren't limited by Utonium being endangered, the Smiths prove too weak to pose anything resembling a physical threat to them, with even their "super-weapon" minivan getting taken out in one punch before the family is quickly and effortlessly beaten down and arrested, never appearing again. Brooding Boy, Gentle Girl: Bud and Julie respectively. Bud's you're typicalemochild whereas his younger sister Julie's an upbeat, albeit twisted example of aGenki Girl. Bullying a Dragon: They actively antagonize the girls to get revenge for the family dinner being ruined and Harold getting arrested (neither of which were really their fault) but prove nowhere near effective or genuinely dangerous to threaten the girls themselves and once they physically confront themthey get beaten down in seconds.

characters.name: The Broccoloids
characters.description: Appear only in the episode "Beat Your Greens". A race of broccoli aliens who try to invade Earth. Alien Invasion: They invade the Earth with brainwashing spores that spread to the vegetables causing those who eat them to become immobile. Badass Cape: The leader of the alien broccoli stands out from the others by wearing a belt and a flowing red cape. The Cameo: Two of them make a non-speaking cameo in the beginning of "Bought and Scold",despite being eaten in their first appearance. Dirty Coward: The only reason they were able to launch their invasion in the first place was by incapacitating the adults beforehand, making it clear they were too afraid to invade otherwise. The leader in particular is left pathetically begging for mercy when cornered by the jaws of the kids.

characters.name: The Sandman
characters.description: A one-shot antagonist inDream Scheme, the Sandman is tasked with putting everyone in the world to sleep each night. Unfortunately, since half the world is awake at any given moment,doing his job means he can never catch so much as a wink of sleep himself. He decides to remedy this by putting everyone on earth into an eternal slumber so he can finally catch some sleep, and the girls have to wake him up and convince him to undo the change. Anti-Villain: He isn't evil at all; the guy just wants to get some sleep for a change, and doesn't even realize he's doing any harm. Amazing Technicolor Population: Has purple skin. Except on his nose, which is blue. The Cameo: After his debut episode in season 2, he's completely absent from the show until "The Powerpuff Girls Rule", where he makes a non-speaking cameo as one of several villains pursuing the Key to the World. The Cobbler's Children Have No Shoes: As mentioned, this is the reason why he puts everyone into an eternal sleep to begin with: So he can finally get a good night's shut-eye himself.

characters.name: Patches
characters.description: Appears only in the episode "Imaginary Fiend". An imaginary friend made up by Mike Believe who proves to be outright malicious. Imaginary Enemy: Patches was made up by Mike due to having trouble socializing with others. Unfortunately, Patches proved to do a lot more harm than good as he started getting Mike in trouble. Takes One to Kill One: The girls' attempts to defeat patches prove fruitless due to being unable to see him. Thus, in order to win, the girls come up with their own imaginary friend to deal with him. Tulpa: Patches initially manifests as Mike's imaginary friend. But as he starts relying on Patches as one of the only people he's comfortable talking to, Patches ends up becoming real enough to start messing with people for real. Villainous Harlequin: Once the Girls make their own imaginary friend to fight him, Patches is revealed to be an unkempt jester with a five o'clock shadow who got his name because of the patches all over his outfit.

characters.name: The Ministry of Pain
characters.description: Art Shift: Just like Captain Righteous and Lefty, theiryounger selves◊are depicted in a more realistic art style reminiscent of theThe Golden Age of Comic Books. Big, Thin, Short Trio: As elderly folks. Counterpart is the big one, Mastermind is the thin one, and Cohort is the short one. Feeling Their Age: Constant cough and bad backs. Their battle against Captain Rightous was quick and anti-climatic, and landed all of them, along with Lefty, in the hospital. Harmless Villain: The only reason the Girls don't simply beat them up is because Blossom doesn't want to injure a bunch of frail geriatrics, something that others don't realize. This leads her to try to get their old nemeses to take them on, which just results in all of them hurting themselves and people getting angry at Blossom. I Was Quite the Looker: Back in their heyday, they were all quite muscular and well-built. EvenCohort, who was already quite short back then.

characters.name: Mike Brikowski
characters.description: Appears in the episode "Cop Out".A lazy copwho gets fired for that reason and tries to kill the girls out of revenge. Abhorrent Alpha Male: Being aDirty Cop, he thinks that he's the best person in the force... when really,he's not. Also, whenever he sees the PPG doing the work, he believes that the trio "[makes] cops look like bums", which is just a pathetic argument for him to boost his ego. All for Nothing: His plan of attempted murder by dunking the Powerpuff Girls in a vat of acid would've been a serious case ofThe Bad Guy Winswhen an officer accidentally fails to stop them from getting dunked... but they're immune to the acid. Brikowski earned himself a one-way trip to prison with nothing to show for it besides the world knowing he's a lousy cop and an attempted murderer. Ambitious, but Lazy: While most characters who fit this trope at least make half-assed efforts in achieving their goals, Brikowski doesn't even bother with that much. He just sat around eating doughnuts and expected a promotion to just behandedto him. Bad "Bad Acting": When lying to the Mayor.

characters.name: Giant Orange Monster
characters.description: Always a Bigger Fish: He's a lumbering, unstoppable monster that is a magnitude stronger than any creature the Girls have faced before. The Giant Orange Monster cannot be overcome with force, but he has a heart, and can be reasoned with to leave people alone. Ambiguous Situation: It's not clear why he returned to Townsville in "Documentary", and the Girls this time wereforcefulin making him leave. It's possible the other monsters don't get along with him, or he's endlessly curious about humans. Anti-Villain: The monster attacking Townsville is a rampaging kaiju, but isn't as bad as he appears since all it takes to stop him was asking him to leave. Being aBruiser with a Soft Centermay also be the reason why he refuses to leave and keeps returning to the city instead of fighting with all the other giant monsters on Monster Isle. Aside Glance: He gives aDisapproving Lookto the viewer, because Buttercup and Blossom stubbornly refuse to learn their lesson and are beginning to bore him. Because You Were Nice to Me: The Giant Orange Monster stops destroying Townsville after Bubbles approaches him and politely asks to stop. You wouldn't think something as intimidating, feral, and gigantic as he would care about manners and beunable to refuse kind requests.

characters.name: The Robbing Leech
characters.description: Actually Not a Vampire: His powers make him seem like one, but he's actually a leech. Affably Evil: While he never talks, his mannerisms imply this. After robbing the Sapphire Sultan of his jewel which he kept in his stomach, he tips his hat in a polite "thank you" gesture. Ambiguously Human: It's hard to tell if he's a superpowered human or something else entirely. Animal Motifs: The leech, obviously. Badass in a Nice Suit: He's a skilled master thief and he rocks a pretty nice suit. Man's got taste.

characters.name: Femme Fatale
characters.description: The third notable villainess in the series, next to Princess Morbucks and Sedusa, despite being a minor villain. She only appears in the episode "Equal Fights" as acowardlyman-bashingStraw Feministwho only stole coins with Susan B. Anthony's portrait on them. Arson, Murder, and Jaywalking: The three women who criticize the Powerpuff Girls for buying her excuse of being a proponent of women's rights are a bank manageress whose bank she robbed, a policewoman whose arm she broke, and a teenage girl whose hairstyle she "copied". Badass Normal: Doesn't have any special powers, is never shown actually fighting, but still holds up banks at gunpoint. Berserk Button: Don't give her any normal U.S. dollar bill. Give her Susan B. Anthony coins or else. Beauty Is Bad: She does have some eye-catching looks, especially when she was unmasked at the end of "Equal Fights", but her insides aremuchuglier than that.

characters.name: Bernie Bernstein
characters.description: A movie director who appeared in "Film-Flam" Alliterative Name: His first and last name both start with B. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He pretends that he's a nice guy who interested in making a movie about the Powerpuff Girls, only for him to reveal his true colors in his trailer and admit that he only wanted to con people. Then again, he does reveal his true colors bit by bit down the road. Con Artist: His plan was to create a fake movie to swindle Townsville out of their money. Jerkass: His true colors slipped out when he angrily told Bubbles to keep her mouth shut.

characters.name: The Nanobots
characters.description: Combining Mecha: When it's clear they are losing to the girls, the remaining nanobots form into one gigantic (actually 6 inches) monobot. Didn't Think This Through: The nanobotscombine into a giant robotin order to defeat the girls with ease. While theyalmost succeed, they fail to account for the fact that by combining and becoming bigger, they've made themselves vulnerable to the evenbigger Grey Goo: The nanobots destroy everything made of carbon, quickly "melting" away Townsville, and use the material to make more of themselves. Hoist by His Own Petard: When trying to take out the girls the nanobots concentrate their entire number into one giant monobot. However, while it's giant to the girls it's only a few inches tall to the rest of the world, and now that it's big enough to see the Professor can easily crush it with his foot. It Can Think: The nanobots, prior to engaging the shrunken girls in battle, seem to be mindless drones that only seek to multiply by consuming carbon. But as more and more of them are destroyed by the girls, they divert their attention from consuming Townsville completely in favor of focusing on killing the girls. The resulting monobot even shows this intent; when the girls are thrashed into the ground, he proceeds to try and squish them under his foot.

characters.name: The Alien
characters.description: Appears only in the episode "Forced Kin". A colossal, metallic alien that seeks to conquer Earth and predicts the Powerpuffs' every move. However at the end, he can't predict Mojo's fury of being evil, and retreats after being defeated by him. Always Someone Better: He's much more competent and evil than Mojo, until he does everything Mojo ever wanted to do to Townsville,causing Mojo to go ballistic. Captain Ersatz: Of Galactus. Both are gigantic evil aliens who threaten Earth. Curb-Stomp Battle: Absolutely defeats the Powerpuff Girls, twice. In terms of evil plans, the Alien outmaneuvered and outsmarted Mojo Jojo completely.Mojo did not take this well, and he managed to curbstomp the Alien. Evil Genius: Effortlessly and flawlessly outpredicts the Powerpuff Girls' attempts to stop his assault, including untested attack patterns. It got to the point that they teamed up with Mojo Jojo in order to outmaneuver him. Even when Mojo and the girls thwarts two attempts to destroy Townsville, Mojo immediately recognizes him as a worthy opponent, until the Alien starts outsmarting Mojohard. Not only performing acts of villainy that Mojo initially planned and wanted to do, but even counteracting Mojo and the girls attempts at counteracting those plans, to the point of breaking Mojo Jojo completely.

characters.name: Dick Hardly
characters.description: Abusive Parents: He treats his creations more like products rather than being a loving father. When his Powerpuff Girlz Xtreme start to become a hit, Dick deliberately cuts off the materials required for them to create more clones, resulting in them being either hideously deformed or prone to breaking apart. When he sees a perfect Buttercup clone amongst the crowd, Dick callously orders his workers to melt it down for its Chemical X. During his fight with the Powerpuff Girls, Dick swipes his creations away while calling them "junk". This mistreatment would later be used against him, as the clones, touched by Professor Utonium's love for the girls, decide to fight back and overwhelm Dick for not showing them any love. All for Nothing: Not only does his plans to have Utonium do his work fail due to his clones deciding to end him to prevent his evil, but context clues heavily imply his business went under due to his poor marketing and shoddy methods to make clones, leaving him without any work force to fall back on, with the strong hints that he was doomed to be bankrupt, even before he became a monster that would make his business ventures even less likely. All Men Are Perverts: Has always been this since his college days, evidently viewing attractive women within his age range as objects to lust over. Ambiguous Situation: When the Girls finally corner him, his previously very productive factory, is entirely vacant aside from himself and his remaining clones despite havingheavily implied to have his staff work long hours to produce his clones at blinding speeds, yet this is lacking. Was it due to him firing them for not managing to work as efficiently as he demanded or them? Or was it due to them having been fed up with his poor business choices and abhorrent treatment of the clones, quitting, not wanting anything to do with his failed business. Ambition Is Evil: His Powerpuff Girls Xtreme business has made him a biggerJerkassthan how he was before.

characters.name: Whimsical Willy
characters.description: Alliterative Name:WhimsicalWilly Broken Pedestal: For Bubbles, once she finds out the truth behind the show. Depraved Kids' Show Host: He turns out to be a greedy con artist who tricks the kids of Townsville into stealing money for him. Monster of the Week: Only appears in "Neighbor Hood", where he was the main antagonist. "Oh, Crap!" Smile: At the end of the episode, he gives a rather scared smile when he realizes that he's in jail and surrounded by inmates ready to beat the crap out of him.

characters.name: Whimsical Willy's friends
characters.description: Adorable Evil Minions: Subverted. All five of them are cute looking (although Kitty is moreUgly Cute), but they just costumes and puppets. Their true appearances are ugly, thuggish men Alliterative Name:MaidMary andDynamiteDog Creepy Crossdresser: Maid Mary is a man. A Dog Named "Cat": Kitty is an elephant, not a cat. Latex Perfection: Maid Mary is wearing a realistic mask. Odd, as he's the only one to do so.

characters.name: The Burglar
characters.description: An oblivious burglar who once tried to rob the Powerpuff Girls' house in "Burglar Alarmed". The Girls would have dealt with him easily, but Professor Utonium needed to sleep for a dissertation, and they didn't want to risk waking him up. Affably Evil: Even if he is robbing their house, the burglar does act nice to the girls, at least before he finds out their true nature. Beard of Evil: He has a little goatee. In the Hood: He wears a black hood over his head. Harmless Villain: He's not really much of a threat, being an ordinary burglar and all, but he ends up getting knocked out by Professor Utoniumwhile he's still asleep.

characters.name: The Gnome
characters.description: A one-shot villain who appeared in the musical episode "See Me, Feel Me, Gnomey". One of the few antagonists in the series that has died. A God Am I: He seemed to believe this, since he had the people of Townsville form a cult and worship him after he destroys the city's villains. Alas, Poor Villain: As he falls to his death, he realizes too late how totally in the wrong he was, andreadily accepts his fate. Allegorical Character: The Gnome is essentially an allegory for the dangers of authoritarianism, totalitarianism, and religious sectarianism. You can see how the episode's message strongly disapproves of a megalomaniacal, egocentric, and sectarian leader who only seeks universal praise. Amazing Technicolor Population: He has pink skin.

characters.name: Dooks of Doom
characters.description: All Bikers Are Hells Angels: They are a biker gang of thuggish, destructive monsters with limited intelligence, who literallyturn the area around them into a wasteland just by passing through. Ax-Crazy: A trio of foaming-at-the-mouth mad maniacs, they are. Badass Biker: Clearly dangerous and strong (even Wizzer casually survives being fired from a tank), though they seem to be rather flexible about what counts as a bike, as Goll-Gorr drives a tank and Wizzer drives a moped. Badass Cape: Hog-Gwarr has an edgy-looking cape that looks quite cool as he rides his chopper. Bad Boss: Goll-Gorr to Wizzer. He pounds him into the shape of a missile and then fires him out of his tank. And judging from the way Wizzer panics and tries to run away when Goll-Gorr says he needs a bomb, he's done this before.

characters.name: Max Von Nitrate
characters.description: A silent movie actor who fell into obscurity because people found his voice ridiculous once he started appearing in sound films. He now wants to take Professor Utonium's voice so he can get his fame back. Anti-Villain: He was one a famous silent movie actor, but when film started using sound, his career was ruined since his voice is high and grating. So he just wants Professor Utonium's voice and means no real harm. Fallen-on-Hard-Times Job: Once one of the greatest stars of the film industry during the silent era, he's now been relegated to working as a simple projectionist playingreruns of his old movies. Heel–Face Turn: Stops being a villain at the end of the episode, when he goes back to being an actor, and has his lines dubbed. Shout-Out: He's a reference to the many silent film stars whose careers didn't survive the transition to talkies, includingDouglas Fairbanksand John Gilbert. His voice being too squeaky for audiences to take seriously is a reference to the longstanding rumor that Gilbert had the same problem.noteIt's now believed that Gilbert's career was more likely derailed due to his feud with MGM mogul Louis B. Mayer and his awkward, affected diction and enunciation in talkies, something which was exacerbated by several bad scripts.His name is a reference to cellulose nitrate, the most widely used base material for film reels in the silent era, which was ultimately phased out due to its volatility and flammability.noteNitrate film decays as it ages, producing flammable gases and becoming increasingly prone to auto-ignition. It wasn't uncommon for the stuff to catch fire in the middle of a movie if it overheated in the projector, and two major fires caused by decaying nitrate film in 1978 wiped out most of the United States' silent film and newsreel archives.It may also be a reference to legendary Swedish-French actorMax von Sydow.

characters.name: The Fluffy Bunch
characters.description: A trio of animals that only appeared in "Sweet N' Sour". They use their adorableness to get away with bad things. Badass Adorable: All of them are cute but they are skilled felons. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: They act innocent and sweet around other people, but when they're alone with the Powerpuff Girls, they are mean. Casting Gag: They all share the PPG's same voice actors. Cute Is Evil: They're undeniably adorable, but don't forget that they are still criminals.

characters.name: Mask Scara
characters.description: A former fashion mogul named Madame M who became the supervillainess when her cosmetic brands have declined in popularity thanks to the Trashy Look overtopping them. Appears only in the episode "A Made Up Story". Alliterative Name: Her previous nameMadameM. Ax-Crazy: Bubbles even calls her "nuts" for her delusional vandalism against Townsville with her make-up brands. Brought Down to Normal: After she was splashed with the Professor's C.O.L.D. Cream, she loses her cosmetic powers, thus everything she has vandalized in Townsville was also brought back to normal. Bullying a Dragon: The fact that she manages to cosmeticizeHIM, the series' demonic entity, isreallysaying something about her.

characters.name: Mojo's Monkey Army
characters.description: Primates from Townsville's local zoo mutated with Chemical X by Mojo Jojo to serve as his army, only for all of them to prove intelligent enough to compete with their own individual plans to rule the world. Fortunately, the Powerpuff Girls manage to put a stop to all of them. The Season 6 episode "Prime Mates" features a former member of the army named Mopey Popo as an antagonist alongside Mojo himself. Rejected when a gorilla damaged his brain, Mopey wanted to help Mojo, but proved to be a nuisance. Eventually, Mopey somehow captures the Powerpuff Girls, but decides to free them and quit being evil. Ax-Crazy: Whacko Smacko, whose idea of destroying Townsville is to go around violently slapping people full force. Badass Army: Even before they started pulling out their various inventions, they almost succeeded in destroying Townsville in the movie had it not been for the girls. Banana Peel: Hacha Chacha's "diabolical" plan is just lobbing banana peels so that everyone in Townsville will slip around.

characters.name: The Powerpunk Girls
characters.description: Mirror Universecounterparts of the Powerpuff Girls who only appeared in Issue 50 of the DC tie-in comics, titled "Deja View". Known for wearing punk-esque outfits (thus, their "Powerpunk" namesake), they live in the City of Vilestown (Townsville's equivalent) at the headquarters of Oppressor Plutonium, Professor Utonium's counterpart who had taken over the city as itsEvil Overlordat some point in the past; according to Jomo Momo (Mojo Jojo's heroic counterpart from the universe), they serve as the enforcers of Plutonium's rule, though they're more motivated for finding it fun to engage in public destruction and other crimes. Individually, their names are Berserk (Blossom's counterpart), Brat (Bubbles) and Brute (Buttercup). In "Deja View", they're taken to the Townsville at same time the Powerpuffs were sent to Vilestown from Bubbles unwittingly creating a time paradox between the mirrors of their respective bedrooms, prompting them to engage in their usual havoc-wrecking ways in Townsville as their fresh new target city. Age-Inappropriate Dress:Brat is a kindergarten-aged girl who wears a midriff-exposing tank top.Brute wears a more modest dress, but also fishnet stockings and spiked wristbands.Additionally, both Brat and Brute have identical footwear that's implied to be leather boots with notably elevated heel. Brat is a kindergarten-aged girl who wears a midriff-exposing tank top. Brute wears a more modest dress, but also fishnet stockings and spiked wristbands.

characters.name: The Micro-Puffs
characters.description: They appear in a trilogy of DC Comics stories comprising Issues 65 ("Meet the Micro-Puffs") and 68 of DC's mainThe Powerpuff Girlscomic ("Micro-Managing"), plus the first story of Issue 23 ofCartoon Network Block Party("The MP Three"). Ambiguously Evil: It's not made clear if they're really asInnocently Insensitiveas they let on, or have more ulterior motives. While they're established as just wanting to stay alongside the Powerpuff Girls, their morality is put a bit into question when they engage inBedtime Brainwashingtowards the Powerpuffs twice. Bedtime Brainwashing:Near the end of "Meet the Micro-Puffs", they whisper to the girls while they're sleeping to convince them that various villains are attacking (or planning to attack) Townsville.In "Micro-Managing", the Micro-Puffs brainwash Bubbles and Buttercup into wanting to be the leader of their team; when Micro-Blossom tries to do the same to Blossom, it doesn't work because Blossom's already the leader. Near the end of "Meet the Micro-Puffs", they whisper to the girls while they're sleeping to convince them that various villains are attacking (or planning to attack) Townsville. In "Micro-Managing", the Micro-Puffs brainwash Bubbles and Buttercup into wanting to be the leader of their team; when Micro-Blossom tries to do the same to Blossom, it doesn't work because Blossom's already the leader.

characters.name: Bliss
characters.description: The fourth (but chronologically first) Powerpuff Girl of the 2016 series, who debuted in the 5-part special episode "Power of Four" from Season 2. In overall terms with the whole franchise, she's the fifth Powerpuff Girl thus far, being preceded by Bunny from the 1998 series' episode "Twisted Sister". A prototypical predecessor (and thus considered the older sister) of Blossom, Bubbles and Buttercup, Bliss is set apart from them for not only having a purple outfit, a blue headband with a pink heart, a darker skin color and unnatural cyan hair, but also for having the physical age of a teenager rather than an elementary child, due to Professor Utonium creating her a decade before her younger sisters. Her mixture of ingredients is mostly the same as the triplets with the exception of being powered from Chemical W, a related variant of Chemical X. In terms of powers, she has all of the collective and individual powers of her sisters in addition to some defining ones of her own, mainly based around the generation and manipulation of electricity. While she's a kind person and is as willing to be a crime-fighter as her sisters (to the point considering such matter as her dream occupation), Bliss is known to be fairly unstable because of Chemical W's functional attributes, with her emotions and powers combining together into explosive results when she's emotionally overwhelmed. Because of this reason, she's insecure and anxious over unwittingly causing mass destruction around her and bringing harm towards her loved ones. Much of her character arc comprised in the debut involves her learning to control her stability. All Your Powers Combined: Her superior power level compared to that of her younger sisters is illustrated in her having all of their superpowers (including those delegated to a specific girl) for herself, topped off by some additional powers of her own. Alphabetical Theme Naming: Just like her sisters and the previousSixth RangersBunny and Bullet, Bliss' name b

characters.name: Schedulebot
characters.description: Broken Record: "(Blank)-time! (Blank)-time! (Blank)-time!" Buried Alive: Or at least "Buried while still functional" as it manages to re-activate itself long enough to crawl out from the ground Buttercup buried him in. One-Winged Angel: He actually has a defense mode built into him that unwittingly activated when Blossom and Buttercup try to erase its memory, turning into a much more threatening force. Robot Buddy: For the professor at least and maybe with Bubbles. But Blossom and Buttercup can't stand the thing.

characters.name: Allegro
characters.description: Acid-Trip Dimension: Allegro's... world, so to speak, looks like what one would see on the ultimate of highs. Affably Evil: Sure is friendly and nice for somebody who's a villain. Anti-Villain: He's not malicious, more so inconsiderate of how his powers affect the people around him and the resulting collateral damage. Beary Funny: A very silly villain, and also takes the form of a panda bear. Bears Are Bad News: Very much with this kind of bear...

characters.name: Manboy
characters.description: Angry White Man: Believes that girls and effeminate menhave turned Townsville into a dystopiathat he needs to reclaim. Arch-Enemy: He views Buttercup as one. Beard of Evil: And he can use his beard to attack people. Defiant to the End: Despite getting beaten to a pulp and thrown into the distance, he continues to mock Buttercup. Dumb Muscle: For his age, his strength is impressive. Too bad he's woefully in over his head when he picks fights with the Powerpuff Girls.

characters.name: The Fashionistas
characters.description: Alliterative Name:Bianca andBarbarusBikini. Ambiguously Related: They're sisters but they're of different species. It's unclear if they're adopted sisters or not. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: In "Bridezilla", Bianca confesses to trying to ruin Barbarus' wedding, but only because she was afraid that Barbarus would leave her. She later comes to terms with it, because it would make her sister happy.Sure, the wedding got called off anyway, but it's still a touching moment. Beauty, Brains, and Brawn: When they are aligned with Mojo Jojo, Bianca is the beauty, he's the brains, and Barbarus is the trio's brawn. Beauty Is Bad: Bianca is attractive, except for those odd eyebrows. She's even prettier when her hair is down.

characters.name: Packrat
characters.description: Advertised Extra: He appears in the "Who’s Got the Power?" music video, suggesting that he’ll be a prominent villain. However, while he’s the main villain of two episodes in season 1, he ends up falling victim toChuck Cunningham Syndrome. He’s completely absent in season 2, and in season 3, he only gets mentioned in one episodenote("Mojo the Great")and makes a minor appearance in another episodenote("Total Eclipse of the Kart"). Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever: Got mutated into a goo-covered, gigantic beast in "Strong Armed" due to toxic waste spilling on him. He's back to normal by the end of the episode after getting caught in an explosion. Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!: Packratlovesshiny things. He’ll steal anything shiny: jewels, anything made of gold or silver, and random shiny objects like hubcaps. Beast Man: He's a big, talking, humanoid rat. The Beastmaster: He has an army of regular rats who obey his orders and act as his minions.

characters.name: Silico
characters.description: Actually a Doombot: Silico is fond of using holograms and other decoys. In “Halt and Catch Silico”, it’s revealed that he’d been a hologram the entire time. Buttercup even Lampshades it as a supervillain cliche. He takes it a step further in “The Troubles With Bubbles”, where he’s implied to have uploaded himself into a computer, and is now capable of making 3D copies of himself. Art Evolution: He wasn’t drawn with ears in his first appears, and his mouth was visible when talking. At Least I Admit It: Wholeheartedly agrees with Buttercup when the latter calls him “messed up”, but blames the girls for it.Buttercup: Dude, you're messed up.Silico: Yes, Iammessed up. Badass Normal: Silico himself isn’t the most imposing figure nor does he possess any superpowers, but he more than makes up for it with his intelligence and has a wide assortment of technology to level the playing field. The Bad Guy Wins: In the episode "Viral Spiral". While the Amoeba Boys were defeated by the girls, Silico’s microchip released a swarm of viruses that transmit data to him.Silico: Ah, Powerpuff Girls, you may have won the battle, but you've already lost thewar.Subverted in "Lights Out". Hethinkshe won, but it's ultimately an illusion conjured by Bubbles.

characters.name: Jemmica Thrash/Jemoiré
characters.description: A new student in adventurer gear that comes to Midway Elementary. Adventurer Archaeologist: Claims she's an amateur one and looks the part. But subverted later as she always gets others to do her work. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Comes off as nice and friendly to the girls but once she gets the first of the idols, she quickly drops it.
